title: Seattle Host City Finances Under Scrutiny: FIFA Takes Venue Revenue While City Bears Security Costs
detail: Analysis of Seattle's financial obligations as a World Cup host city reveals a stark imbalance: FIFA collects stadium venue revenues while the city shoulders infrastructure, security, and logistics costs. The arrangement raises questions about net public benefit for taxpayers ahead of the tournament, a pattern repeated across all 16 host cities in the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

title: Spain Name 26-Man World Cup Squad — Zero Real Madrid Players for First Time in World Cup History; Eight Barcelona Stars; Gavi Returns
detail: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente announced the 26-man squad at Espacio Movistar (Edificio Telefónica, Gran Vía 28, Madrid) on May 25 — making history by selecting zero Real Madrid players, the first time Spain has named a World Cup squad with no Real Madrid representatives. Neither Dani Carvajal (injured) nor Joan García-Huijsen made the cut, reflecting Real Madrid's disappointing 2025–26 season and a broader shift toward Barcelona's resurgent generation. Eight Barcelona players were named in the squad. Key inclusions: Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, still fit despite pre-announcement uncertainty), Pedri (Barcelona), Rodri (Manchester City, captain), Nico Williams (Athletic Club), Gavi (Barcelona, returning from a lengthy injury absence), and Dani Olmo (Barcelona). De la Fuente also named nine 'support players' — includung Real Madrid's Gonzalo García and Barcelona's Marc Bernal — who will train with the squad during the pre-tournament camp but are not in the final 26. Spain open Group H: vs Mexico (June 14, Hard Rock Stadium Miami), vs Peru (June 19, Globe Life Field Arlington), vs Tunisia (June 24, Bank of America Stadium Charlotte). 17 days to kickoff at Estadio Azteca.

title: Mexico Confirms It Will Host Iran's National Team During World Cup — Sheinbaum: 'No Issue' as US Denies Visas
detail: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed on May 25 that Mexico has 'no issue' with hosting Iran's national football team during the 2026 World Cup, after FIFA approached Mexico as an alternative base camp option. Iran's football federation confirmed its delegation will base from Tijuana, Mexico — directly across the US border from San Diego — after the United States failed to grant visas to any Iranian delegation member. Iran will commute across the border for their three group-stage matches in the US: SoFi Stadium in Inglewood (June 15 vs New Zealand; June 21 vs Belgium) and Lumen Field in Seattle (June 26 vs Egypt). The Tijuana base 'includes all training facilities, gym, private restaurant, and everything the team needs,' according to Iran's federation. This arrangement represents an unprecedented logistical situation for a World Cup: a national team based in a neighboring country and commuting internationally for each match. Mexico City also announced new health protocols in response to the Ebola situation, implementing epidemiological surveillance and sanitary filters for tourists arriving from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

media.caption: Mexico confirms it will host Iran's national team during the World Cup — Iran to base from Tijuana as US fails to issue visas
